chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two (peace be upon them), regarding

a man who confessed to adultery four times, and he was married (muhsan), that he would be stoned until he dies, or he denies himself before being stoned, saying 'I did not do it'. So if he says that, he is left alone and is not stoned.
And he (peace be upon him) said: The thief is not cut until he confesses to the theft twice. So if he retracts, he guarantees the theft, and is not cut if there are no witnesses.
And he (peace be upon him) said: The adulterer is not stoned until he confesses four times to adultery, if there are no witnesses. So if he retracts, he is left alone and is not stoned.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for waiving the stoning penalty for a married adulterer who confesses?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'al-ijtibab bi al-iqrar' (voluntary confession) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that a single individual's repeated self-incrimination suffices for hudud penalties even without witnesses. It highlights the legal nuance that retraction (ruju') before the penalty is fully executed nullifies the punishment, reflecting the Shia preference for caution in applying fixed penalties. This ruling underscores the high evidentiary threshold required for hudud, distinguishing between the requirements for theft (two confessions) and adultery (four confessions).
